Query pushdown and materialization A Polars LazyFrame delays execution, but the database can only reduce its work when optimizer hints cross the I/O boundary. fsspec-polars translates those hints through the Polars I/O plugin interface. Relation paths and SQL take different routes Relation scans encode selected columns, predicates, and row limits in an fsspec-db path. SQL scans already have a query, so optional helpers rewrite that query instead. Both return Arrow data that becomes a Polars DataFrame. Local fallback preserves filter order When a predicate cannot be translated, the scan reads the columns needed to filter locally and delays projection and row limiting until after that filter. Applying a row limit before an unsupported filter could discard rows that should have matched. This preserves results but may require reading the complete relation or query result. A LazyFrame or a final .limit() does not by itself guarantee a bounded database read. Lazy scans still materialize backend results Relation scans call cat_file and decode the returned Arrow IPC bytes. SQL scans call query and receive a complete Arrow table. When a predicate cannot be translated, the scan reads the columns needed to filter locally and delays projection and row limiting until after that filter. Applying a row limit before an unsupported filter could discard rows that should have matched. This preserves results but may require reading the complete relation or query result. A LazyFrame or a final .limit() does not by itself guarantee a bounded database read.

s: Lazy scans still materialize backend results
x: Relation scans call cat_file and decode the returned Arrow IPC bytes. SQL scans call query and receive a complete Arrow table. Frame slicing into requested batch sizes happens after that materialization; it is not database streaming. Schema inference can also contact the database during LazyFrame construction. An explicit schema avoids that query, while making the caller responsible for its accuracy. Repeated collections can execute the source again. See How to scan relations and SQL for configuration and the scan reference for both function contracts.

Install the backend and any driver required by your fsspec-db protocol. Scan a relation import polars as pl from fsspec_polars import scan_db_relation users = scan_db_relation( "db+sqlite", "/main/users", storage_options={"database": "app.db"}, ) result = users.filter(pl.col("score") > 2).select("name").limit(10).collect() Reuse a filesystem and schema Pass filesystem= when an application already owns the database connection. scan_db_sql(protocol, sql, *, storage_options=None, filesystem=None, schema=None, dialect=None) Common parameters have the same meaning as in scan_db_relation. sql is the source SQL; surrounding whitespace and one trailing semicolon are removed. The filesystem must implement query(sql) returning a pyarrow.Table. Without schema, construction runs: SELECT * FROM (<source SQL>) AS __fsspec_polars_schema LIMIT 0 When pushdown helpers are available, source SQL can be wrapped with optimizer projection, predicates, and limits. Otherwise the source query runs unchanged and Polars operations are applied locally. SQLite expression and aggregate columns can have different inferred dtypes in a zero-row query and a populated result. An explicit schema supplies the expected dtypes when the backend cannot infer them consistently.

scan_kafka(path, *, storage_options=None, filesystem=None) Parameter Meaning path: str Topic, such as kafka://orders, or one partition, orders/0. storage_options: Mapping | None fsspec-kafka options, such as bootstrap.servers and value format. filesystem Existing filesystem; takes precedence over storage_options. Requires fsspec-kafka. Construction reads topic/_meta/watermarks.json for the partitions and their offset ranges, and a zero-message read of the first partition for the schema. Each partition is then read as topic/partition.arrow?start=&limit=. With the pushdown extra, predicates narrow those reads. partition == and partition.is_in skip partitions, comparisons on offset set start and limit, and a lower bound on timestamp reads topic/partition/@timestamp.arrow instead. Converting time-zone-aware timestamps needs time zone data, which the extra installs on Windows as tzdata. Other predicates, including |, read whole partitions. The full predicate is always applied to the rows read. A row limit stops reading further partitions, but each partition is read whole, because compaction leaves gaps between offsets.

Protocol Inferred dialect db+sqlite sqlite db+postgres, db+postgresql postgres db+mysql mysql Other None The pushdown extra supplies polars-io-tools and sqlglot. Relation projection and row-limit hints do not require the extra when no predicate needs local fallback. SQL rewriting requires the extra. Database, codec, and expression errors propagate from the underlying libraries.
